title: Needleboard microtrial sheet — Aria
content:
Needleboard microtrial sheet — scratchpad for quick trials
Owner: Aria Chen (personal tracker)
Purpose: tiny table to keep per-session trial summary, quick metrics, and immediate next steps. Meant for fast capture during iterations, not polished.

---
KEY HYPOTHESIS / NOTES TO SELF:
- Small precision of batching + early prefix caching gives 10-20% p95 wins on short prompts (<=120 tokens).
- Watch for regressions when quantization changes (int8 vs q4) — sometimes p50 improves but p95 spikes.
- If p95 > 220ms do a slow-path trace (KV growth?).

EXPERIMENT TABLE (latest first) — columns: date, run_id, model, variant, batch_size, quant, seq_len, tokens_run, p50_ms, p95_ms, cost_per_1k, success?, notes
2025-09-03, nb-0923-a, redwood-llama-13b, opt-slim, 4, q4_0.5, 128, 18.5k, 37, 235, $0.085, partial, p95 jump on long-tail; trace shows cold KV miss at step ~45
2025-09-02, nb-0922-e, redwood-llama-13b, opt-slim, 8, int8, 64, 24.0k, 30, 190, $0.070, ok, good p95 but cost up slightly; try q4 run next
2025-08-30, nb-0830-c, redwood-mistral-7b, default, 16, q4_0.5, 96, 40.2k, 22, 120, $0.045, yes, stable, consider increasing batch to 24
2025-08-25, nb-0825-b, redwood-llama-13b, fallback-cpu, 1, fp16, 128, 4.6k, 250, 1200, $0.60, no, unacceptable latency — fallback path used during outage; file ticket
2025-06-25, nb-0625-x, redwood-llama-33b, opt-slim, 2, q5_0.8, 256, 6.1k, 120, 540, $0.30, partial, memory pressure + KV thrashing observed

QUICK METRICS SNAPSHOT (rolling last 7 runs):
- mean(p50) = 88 ms
- mean(p95) = 257 ms (high variance, median p95=210)
- mean cost/1k = $0.162

ACTIONS / NEXT STEPS (short list):
- [ ] Re-run nb-0923-a with smaller batch (2) to see if p95 drop — suspected batching interference with prefix caching.
- [ ] Add microtrace hook to capture per-step KV size for any run crossing p95 > 300ms. (ticket: JIRA-ENG-1289)
- [ ] Run q4_0.5 and q5_0.8 side-by-side on 13b with seq_len 128, batch 4 — measure output quality delta (& embed similarity).
- [ ] Share two-row summary with Kai for dedupe on infra change window (he's collab)

RUNDOWN / QUICK OBSERVATIONS (bullet notes, noisy):
- On 9/3 the p95 spike looks correlated with a single request pattern (long context + many short completions). Might be a batching mixing issue.
- Fallback-cpu path kills p95 and cost; need clearer routing policy for critical routes (degrade gracefully to smaller model rather than CPU).
- q4 seems promising for cost but watch tail latency.

RAW RUN CHECKLIST (adhoc)
- run id in logs? -> yes, tag nb-XXXX in all runners
- save trace? -> only for runs flagged partial/no
- snapshot model config -> embed in run artifact (commit hash)

SNIPPET: quick csv export (copy-paste to sheet)

2025-09-02,nb-0922-e,redwood-llama-13b,opt-slim,8,int8,64,24000,30,190,0.070,yes,"good p95"

OPEN QUESTIONS (to resolve later):
- Is there a correlation between request-level token distribution skew and p95 outliers? need to sample request histograms.
- Are certain prompt templates causing KV inflation? run per-template ablation.

END NOTE: keep this minimal — if something looks worth formalizing move to shared_drives/engineering/observability/ or product/optimize. This file is my day-to-day needleboard for quick captures.
